title: [Prototype] I'm building an AI-powered detective interrogation game — looking for honest feedback!
author: ataidefilipe
selftext:
Hey everyone!

I've been working on a prototype for Detective AI, a criminal investigation game where you interrogate AI-driven suspects in natural language, present evidence to catch contradictions and break their alibis, build a case file, and make your final accusation.



I'd love for you to try it out and share your honest feedback:

👉 [https://detective-ai-production.up.railway.app](https://detective-ai-production.up.railway.app)



A few heads-ups before you jump in:

\* Early prototype: Things are still rough around the edges, and I'm actively iterating on the mechanics and UX.

\* Partially in Portuguese: I started building this project in Portuguese, so some parts of the UI/content are still in PT-BR while I work on translating everything.

\* Bring Your Own API Key: Since I'm hosting this as a solo prototype, you'll need to enter your own OpenAI API key (\`sk-...\`) in the settings to run the AI interrogations.



What I'd love feedback on:

\* Does the interrogation loop feel fun and intuitive?

\* Did presenting evidence to break lies work the way you expected?

\* Any bugs, confusing UI moments, or pacing issues?



Thanks a lot to anyone who gives it a shot!

This post may be removed if it isn't updated.

replies.author: ataidefilipe
replies.body: Sorry about that. I completely missed Rule 4 when posting. I've updated the post with details on how the AI architecture and development process work!

comments.author: True_Woodpecker2118
comments.body: Idk how to do any of that. Im a noob. But i had a peak, and it could be quite compelling, quick question. Will failing cases and or letting certain suspects get away. Effect future cases and choices?

replies.author: ataidefilipe
replies.body:
Thanks for checking it out! That's actually a really cool idea.

Right now cases are self-contained, so failing one or letting a suspect slip away doesn't carry over yet, but having those consequences ripple into future cases and choices would make the investigation loop way more compelling. I'm definitely adding that to the backlog!

I'm also planning to open up a space where players can build and share their own cases, so if you ever want to try designing a mystery yourself without touching code, that'll be an option down the road.
